zh.summary: 先用兩筆合成資料檢查成品，再把畫面、業務規則與交付證據連起來。你將能指出原型已做到什麼，以及下一個需要驗證的問題。
objectives: 用具體任務描述軟體成果，而非只列出畫面或工具。
區分功能展示、規格驗證、使用者驗收與正式上線。
從一次缺漏檢核追溯需求、實作、測試與交接作品。

sections.heading: 第一課：先看成品，從問題到成果
paragraphs: 這堂課最重要的觀念是：軟體工程不是把程式寫出來，而是用程式解決一個問題，並且證明這個問題真的被解決了。
以前我們可能認為，軟體開發就是工程師寫程式，寫完能執行，就算完成。
但在 AI 時代，AI 可能只要幾分鐘就能產生一個有畫面、有按鈕、有功能的網站。這時候真正困難的事情，反而變成：
「我們怎麼知道 AI 做出來的東西，真的是使用者需要的？」
這就是本課的核心。

sections.heading: 一、寫出網站，不代表解決問題
paragraphs: 假設今天有一位承辦人，每天都要收到許多申請文件。
有些人忘記填申請編號，有些人忘記填文件類型。承辦人必須逐一檢查，既浪費時間，也可能漏看。
現在我們請 AI 幫忙。
兩個網站可能看起來都很漂亮，但只有第二個真正針對承辦人的問題設計。
這裡涉及軟體工程的一個基礎概念：Problem Definition（問題定義）。
我們要先知道：
Who（誰）：誰會使用這個系統？
Problem（問題）：他目前遇到什麼困難？
Outcome（成果）：什麼情況下，才算把困難解決？
以這個例子來說，目標不是「增加一個檢查按鈕」，而是「避免承辦人把未填齊的申請誤認為完整」。
為什麼重要？ 因為 AI 能夠產生程式，但 AI 並不一定知道真實的業務需求。沒有清楚的問題定義，AI 很可能把錯誤的方向做得非常精緻。

blocks.caption: 圖 1｜比較表單外觀與成果證據
blocks.description: 兩張卡是平行比較；圖示依附圖的輸入框、主要按鈕、必填標記、錯誤摘要與欄位提示重新設計，不表示已驗收任何實際系統。

items.title: 只關注畫面｜做一個漂亮的表單網站
items.body: 有輸入框、送出與次要操作按鈕，但尚未提供防止漏填的證據。

items.title: 關注實際成果｜做一個能攔截缺漏的工具
items.body: 缺少必填資料時，同時顯示錯誤摘要與欄位提示，並阻止匯出完整報告。

sections.heading: 二、什麼叫做真的做對？我們直接操作看看
paragraphs: 假設規定申請編號、申請人代號、文件類型都是必填欄位。
這裡有兩個情境，你可以點選比較。
你應該注意到一件事：
「欄位檢查通過」與「正式申請核准」完全是兩回事。
想像醫院掛號系統，病患姓名、生日、電話都填了，並不代表病患身分已經確認，更不代表醫療服務已經完成。
所以，系統中的「成功」、「完整」、「完成」等文字，都應有明確定義。
這其實也是 UI／UX 與 HCI（Human–Computer Interaction，人機互動）的重要觀念：系統顯示的狀態，必須讓使用者產生正確的理解，而不是錯誤的信心。

sections.heading: 三、如何把想法變成軟體？理解四類重要文件
paragraphs: 你可以把軟體開發想像成蓋一棟房子。
蓋房子之前，我們要知道住戶需求，接著有設計圖，再由工人施工，最後還要驗收。
軟體工程也是一樣。
我們用最白話的方式理解：
problem.md：問題說明書。 它告訴團隊為什麼需要開發這個工具。例如：「承辦人經常收到資料缺漏的申請，人工檢查容易遺漏。」
spec.md：規格說明書。 它把需求變成明確規則。例如：「只要文件類型空白，就必須顯示錯誤訊息，且禁止匯出完整報告。」
app.py：實際執行的程式。 它把上述規則寫進軟體。當使用者點下檢查，程式就判斷欄位是否符合要求。
tests/：測試。 它檢查程式是不是真的遵守規格，而不只是看起來有這個功能。
README：使用與維護說明書。 它告訴其他工程師這個軟體怎麼安裝、怎麼啟動、怎麼測試，以及有哪些限制。
請特別記住：文件並非為了增加工作量，而是為了讓每個人的理解可以互相核對。
如果規格說不能匯出，但程式卻允許匯出，那就是程式沒有符合規格。
如果程式能攔下缺漏，但測試從來沒有檢查過這個情境，就缺少了對應的測試證據。

blocks.caption: 圖 2｜軟體工程的證據鏈（Traceability）；箭頭表示需求、規格、實作與驗證的追溯關係，後續仍可回頭修訂。

items.title: problem.md：需求
items.body: 收件人員希望在交接前知道缺少哪些必要欄位。

items.title: spec.md：承諾
items.body: 缺少文件類型時，列出缺漏，不能匯出完整報告。

items.title: app.py：實作
items.body: 表單與業務規則依同一份規格處理輸入。

items.title: tests/ 與 README：證據及交接
items.body: 保留缺漏與完整兩種結果，說明如何重現及目前限制。

sections.heading: 四、AI 說完成了，等於真的完成嗎？
paragraphs: 不一定。
這裡要建立一個非常重要的工程觀念：軟體完成有不同層次。
其中，第二與第三層尤其容易混淆。
Verification：我們有沒有把東西做對？
例如規格要求「文件類型缺漏不得匯出」，測試確認程式確實阻止匯出。
Validation：我們有沒有做出真正需要的東西？
例如承辦人使用後，是否能比原來更準確地發現缺漏，而且不會把「欄位檢查通過」誤解為「正式核准」。
一個系統可以通過所有預先寫好的測試，卻仍然不符合使用者需求。因為最初的需求或規格本身可能就有問題。
這也解釋了為什麼只看 AI 的測試結果，還不能完全取代人類驗收。

blocks.caption: 表 1｜完成層次與證據
rows: 1. 展示 Demo
我自己的電腦跑得起來
啟動與實際操作
2. 驗證 Verification
程式符合事先寫好的規格
測試結果
3. 驗收 Validation / UAT
真正的使用者能完成工作
使用者實際操作及驗收紀錄
4. 正式上線 Production
可以提供真實環境使用並維護
部署、權限、安全、備份、監控等檢查

blocks.heading: Streamlit AppTest 能做什麼？
paragraphs: Streamlit 是使用 Python 製作互動式應用的工具；AppTest 則可以模擬使用者輸入及操作，檢查程式產生的結果。
例如讓程式自動檢查：當文件類型空白時，是否顯示缺漏提示。
但 AppTest 不能僅靠程式測試就證明承辦人理解這個提示，更無法單靠它證明整個系統已符合正式環境的資安要求。
另外還有一個工程細節：就算畫面上的「匯出」按鈕被停用，也不代表後端一定安全。真正的匯出功能仍應在伺服器端重新確認權限與資料狀態，避免有人繞過畫面直接呼叫 API。

sections.heading: 五、AI Coding Agent 與人類應該怎麼分工？
paragraphs: 你可以把 Coding Agent 想成一位能寫程式、修改檔案和執行測試的工程助手。
但我們不能只說「幫我做一個系統」，然後把所有決策都交給 AI。
比較可靠的工作流程是：
人類確認需求與業務規則
決定哪些欄位必填、什麼情況可以匯出、哪些資料不能使用。
AI 根據規格實作與測試
在允許的檔案範圍內寫程式、執行測試、報告通過與失敗的結果。
人類審查 Diff 與測試證據
Diff 是修改前後的差異。確認 AI 沒有改到不該改的地方，也沒有自行改寫需求。
人類決定是否驗收與上線
確認使用者任務、資料安全、維護責任與部署條件，而不只依賴 AI 的完成宣告。
這不代表人類必須親自寫每一行程式，而是即使把實作交給 AI，仍然要保有定義目標、檢查證據及決定是否接受成果的能力。

sections.heading: 六、這堂課與往後軟體工程知識有什麼關係？
paragraphs: M01-01 是整門課的起點，因為它建立了一條可以延伸到各個領域的主軸：
你會發現，這些領域都不是獨立存在的。它們共同處理的是同一件事：如何讓一個軟體成果從想法走向可信任、可使用、可維護的系統。

blocks.caption: 表 2｜後續領域與本課的關係
rows: Requirements Engineering 需求工程
怎麼知道真正要解決什麼問題
UI／UX／HCI
怎麼讓使用者正確理解與操作
Software Design 軟體設計
怎麼規劃程式結構與功能
Testing 軟體測試
怎麼提出證據證明程式符合規格
Cybersecurity 資安
怎麼防止越權、資料外洩及不安全操作
DevOps／Deployment 部署維運
怎麼讓軟體可靠地提供他人使用
AI Agent Governance 代理治理
怎麼限制 AI 的行動權限、審查修改及追蹤責任

sections.heading: 七、理解檢核：用實際情境判斷
paragraphs: 某位同事使用 AI 做了一個申請資料檢查系統。
AI 回報：「已經完成！網站可以開啟，表單可以輸入，按鈕也可以點擊。」
但你還沒有看過測試報告，也沒有請承辦人實際操作。
請問，此時最合理的工程判斷是什麼？
選項與參考解析見下方「理解檢核」。
本課最值得記住的三個字是「可驗證」。 不只要能展示功能，還要說清楚功能符合哪一項需求、用什麼方法檢查，以及哪些事情尚未驗證。
當你能清楚區分「AI 寫好了」、「程式跑起來」、「符合規格」、「使用者驗收通過」與「可以正式上線」，就已經掌握 AI 協作軟體工程最重要的基本判斷能力。

exercise.environment: 紙筆或本機文字編輯器；只用下列合成資料，不需安裝 Agent。
steps: 建立一份成品觀察紀錄，列出 SYN-001、DEMO-A、文件類型空白的預期結果。
再列出三欄皆有值的預期結果，明寫「完整」的教學定義。
將每項預期分別連到 problem.md、spec.md、app.py 或 tests/，指出你目前實際擁有哪些證據。

exercise.check: 請同儕讀你的紀錄：他能否在不猜測的情況下說出缺漏時能不能匯出完整報告？若不能，補寫規則。
exercise.cleanup: 保留合成紀錄供 M03 使用；不要填入真實收件資料。

en.summary: Check a product with two synthetic inputs, then connect its interface, business rules and delivery evidence. Identify what the prototype already does and the next question that needs verification.
objectives: Describe a software outcome through a concrete task, beyond a list of screens or tools.
Distinguish feature demonstrations, specification verification, user acceptance and production release.
Trace one missing-data check through requirements, implementation, tests and handoff artifacts.

sections.heading: Lesson 1: See the Product First, from Problem to Outcome
paragraphs: The central idea of this lesson is that software engineering uses software to solve a problem and provides evidence that the problem has actually been solved.
We may previously have treated software development as engineers writing code: once the code ran, the work was done.
With AI, a website with screens, buttons and working features may be generated in minutes. The difficult question then becomes:
“How do we know that what AI built is what users actually need?”
That question is the focus of this lesson.

sections.heading: 1. Building a Website Does Not Establish That the Problem Is Solved
paragraphs: Imagine an administrator who receives many application documents every day.
Some applicants omit the application ID; others omit the document type. Checking each application takes time, and omissions may still be missed.
Now we ask AI for help.
Both websites may look polished, but only the second design directly addresses the administrator’s problem.
This introduces a basic software engineering concept: problem definition.
First establish:
Who: who will use this system?
Problem: what difficulty do they currently face?
Outcome: what observable situation would count as resolving that difficulty?
In this example, the goal is to prevent the administrator from mistaking an incomplete application for a complete one. Adding a check button alone does not define that outcome.
AI can generate code without knowing the actual business need. Without a clear problem definition, it may produce a very polished implementation in the wrong direction.

blocks.caption: Figure 1 | Compare form appearance with evidence of an outcome
blocks.description: The cards are parallel alternatives. The supplied images inform the input fields, primary button, required markers, error summary and field-level feedback; they do not establish acceptance of an actual system.

items.title: Focus on appearance | Build a polished form website
items.body: Input fields, submit and secondary-action buttons are present, but there is no evidence yet that omissions are prevented.

items.title: Focus on the outcome | Build a tool that catches omissions
items.body: Missing required data triggers an error summary and field-level feedback, and blocks complete-report export.

sections.heading: 2. What Does Getting It Right Mean? Try Two Scenarios
paragraphs: For this example, application ID, applicant code and document type are all required.
Compare the following two scenarios using the controls.
Notice this distinction:
“Field check passed” and “application officially approved” are entirely different states.
In a hospital registration system, entering a patient’s name, date of birth and phone number does not establish verified identity or completed medical care.
Words such as “success,” “complete” and “done” therefore need explicit definitions.
This is also a UI/UX and HCI (Human–Computer Interaction) concern: the displayed state should support an accurate understanding rather than misplaced confidence.

sections.heading: 3. From an Idea to Software: Four Groups of Artifacts
paragraphs: Think of software development as building a house.
Before construction, we learn what the occupants need, prepare a design, carry out the work and finally inspect the result.
Software engineering follows a similar relationship.
In plain language:
problem.md is the problem statement. It explains why the tool is needed: for example, “Administrators frequently receive applications with missing data, and manual checks can overlook omissions.”
spec.md is the specification. It turns the need into an explicit rule: “When document type is blank, display an error and prevent complete-report export.”
app.py is the running program. It implements the rules: when the user checks the application, the program determines whether the required fields are present.
tests/ contains tests. They check whether the program follows the specification, rather than merely appearing to offer a feature.
README explains use and maintenance: how another engineer can install, start and test the software, and what limits apply.
Documents let people cross-check their understanding. That is the purpose of keeping them.
If the specification prohibits export but the program permits it, the implementation does not meet the specification.
If the program blocks omissions but no test covers that case, the corresponding test evidence is missing.

blocks.caption: Figure 2 | Software engineering traceability. Arrows connect requirements, specification, implementation and verification; later revisions can return to earlier artifacts.
blocks.description: Read the numbered steps in order.

items.title: problem.md: the need
items.body: Intake staff need to know which required fields are missing before handoff.

items.title: spec.md: the promise
items.body: When document type is missing, list the omission and prevent complete-report export.

items.title: app.py: the implementation
items.body: The form and business rules process input according to the same specification.

items.title: tests/ and README: evidence and handoff
items.body: Retain incomplete and complete results, reproduction instructions and current limits.

sections.heading: 4. Does an AI Completion Claim Mean the Work Is Done?
paragraphs: Not necessarily.
Software completion has several distinct levels.
The second and third levels are especially easy to confuse.
Verification asks: did we build it according to the specification?
For example, the specification prohibits export when document type is missing, and a test confirms that export is blocked.
Validation asks: did we build what people actually need?
For example, can the administrator find omissions more accurately than before, without mistaking “field check passed” for “official approval”?
A system can pass every predefined test and still fail to meet user needs because the original requirements or specification may themselves be wrong.
That is why AI-reported test results cannot fully replace human acceptance.

blocks.caption: Table 1 | Completion levels and their evidence
rows: 1. Demo
It runs on my computer.
Startup and actual operation.
2. Verification
The program meets the written specification.
Test results.
3. Validation / UAT
Real users can complete the task.
Observed user operation and acceptance records.
4. Production
It can be used and maintained in its real environment.
Deployment, permissions, security, backups and monitoring checks.

blocks.heading: What Can Streamlit AppTest Do?
paragraphs: Streamlit is a Python tool for building interactive applications. AppTest simulates user input and actions and inspects the results produced by the program.
For example, an automated test can check whether a missing-document-type message appears when the field is blank.
AppTest alone cannot establish that the administrator understands the message or that the entire system meets production security requirements.

Disabling an export button also does not establish backend security. A real export endpoint must recheck permissions and data state on the server, including when someone bypasses the interface and calls an API directly.

sections.heading: 5. How Should Coding Agents and People Divide the Work?
paragraphs: Think of a Coding Agent as an engineering assistant that can write code, edit files and run tests.
A request to “build a system” does not provide enough direction to delegate every decision to AI.
A more reliable workflow is:
People confirm requirements and business rules.
Decide which fields are required, when export is permitted and which data may not be used.
AI implements and tests against the specification.
It writes within the permitted file scope, runs tests and reports both passing and failing results.
People review the diff and test evidence.
A diff shows the changes between versions. Check that AI did not modify files outside the scope or silently redefine the requirements.
People decide whether to accept and release the result.
Confirm user tasks, data security, maintenance responsibilities and deployment conditions, rather than relying solely on an AI completion claim.
People need not write every line themselves. Even when AI implements the software, people retain the ability to define goals, examine evidence and decide whether to accept the result.

sections.heading: 6. How Does This Lesson Connect to Software Engineering?
paragraphs: M01-01 begins the course by establishing a thread that extends into several areas:
These areas work together to move software from an idea to a trustworthy, usable and maintainable system.

blocks.caption: Table 2 | Later topics and their connection to this lesson
rows: Requirements Engineering
Identify the real problem to solve.
UI/UX/HCI
Help users understand and operate the system correctly.
Software Design
Plan the software structure and features.
Testing
Provide evidence that the implementation meets its specification.
Cybersecurity
Prevent unauthorized actions, data leaks and unsafe operations.
DevOps / Deployment
Make software reliably available to others.
AI Agent Governance
Constrain agent authority, review changes and trace responsibility.

sections.heading: 7. Check Your Understanding with a Practical Situation
paragraphs: A colleague uses AI to build an application-data checking system.
The AI reports: “Done! The website opens, the form accepts input and the buttons can be clicked.”
You have not seen a test report or asked the administrator to operate it.
What is the most reasonable engineering judgment at this point?
See the choices and reference explanations in the understanding check below.
Remember “verifiable”: identify the requirement a feature meets, how it is checked and what remains unverified, as well as demonstrating the feature.

Distinguishing “AI wrote it,” “it runs,” “it meets the specification,” “users accepted it” and “it is ready for production” gives you a fundamental judgment skill for AI-assisted software engineering.

exercise.environment: Paper or a local text editor. Use only the synthetic data below; no agent installation is needed.
steps: Create a product observation record with the expected result for SYN-001, DEMO-A and a blank document type.
Record the expected result when all three fields have values, explicitly defining “complete” for this exercise.
Link each expectation to problem.md, spec.md, app.py or tests/, and state which evidence you actually have.
exercise.expected: Two input scenarios, an explicit completeness definition, and a mapping of artifacts to evidence.
exercise.check: Ask a peer to read the record: can they tell, without guessing, whether incomplete input may produce a complete report? If not, add the missing rule.

en.prompt: AI reports that the website opens, accepts form input and has clickable buttons. You have not seen tests or observed the administrator using it. What is the most reasonable engineering judgment?
options: The system is complete and ready for colleagues to use in production.
It can at least be demonstrated; the specification and user tasks still need checking.
Because AI says it is done, AI should take responsibility for all acceptance.
If the screen has no typos, the tests can be considered passed.
rationales: A demonstration does not establish specification compliance, user tasks or deployment and maintenance conditions.
B matches the demonstration evidence. Next check the omission-blocking rule and observe the administrator completing the task.
People still confirm business rules, review diffs, interpret evidence and decide whether to accept the result.
Copyediting cannot replace specification tests or user acceptance.
